output.question: What are the key takeaways from Anthropic's S-1 filing?
output.answer: Anthropic, PBC filed its S-1 publicly on Oct. 26, 2026, after a confidential draft on June 1. It plans to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "ANT," with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the deal. As of Nov. 11, an updated filing reportedly offers 825 million shares at $70–$78 each, which would value the company at about $1.4 trillion. The roadshow began Nov. 10, pricing could come as early as Nov. 13, and the stock would likely start trading Nov. 19 or 20. On the numbers, revenue for the first half of 2026 was $16.29 billion, up 1,304%, and $33.2 billion for the first nine months. Implied gross margin rose to about 85%. The first-half net loss was $80.7 billion, but about $72 billion of that was a non-cash accounting charge from convertible notes. The operating loss for the nine months narrowed to $1.3 billion. Other headline items are very large compute commitments (about $417 billion owed to providers, with Amazon, Google, SpaceX and Microsoft as the main contracts), a Founder LLC holding 50.1% of the votes, net revenue retention of about 900%, and over 90 pages of risk factors, including the dispute with the Pentagon and the Trump administration.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO of Class A common stock to list on Nasdaq Global Select Market under 'ANT'. Share count and price were not yet set at filing. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the contacts for the prospectus. A confidential draft was submitted June 1, 2026.

Revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $16.29B, up 1,304% from $1.16B. Full-year 2025 revenue was $4.59B. 80% of revenue was consumption-based and 20% subscription. 27.8% was international.

Implied gross margin was about 85%, up from 12% a year earlier. The H1 2026 net loss was $80.7B, compared with $12.9B a year earlier. About $72B of the loss came from accounting charges on convertible notes as the company's valuation rose.

Future compute obligations to providers total about $417B, plus another $125–150B ordered for 2028–2031 delivery. Noncancelable purchase commitments were $265.6B at June 30, up from $54.6B at year-end 2025. The main contracts are SpaceX (up to $120.5B), Amazon (at least $110B through 2036), Google TPUs ($114.5B through 2033) and Microsoft (at least $44.9B).

Net revenue retention was about 900% as of Sept. 30. About 1,900 customers pay $1M+ and about 250 pay $10M+. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue. Cloud marketplaces accounted for 48% of H1 revenue.

Founder LLC, made up of seven co-founders including Dario and Daniela Amodei, holds 50.1% of voting power, a structure the filing says has 'no direct public company precedent'. Amazon's stake is capped at 12% and is nonvoting. Lock-ups expire in stages at 27, 48, 62 and 76 days after the IPO.

Risk factors run to more than 90 pages. They include disputes with the Trump administration and the Pentagon (the D.C. Circuit ruled for the Defense Department), compute shortfalls, reliance on TSMC, data center moratoriums under consideration in 16 states, and liability if models are misused to build weapons.

Offering: 825M shares at $70–$78, about a $1.4T valuation. The roadshow began Nov. 10, pricing could come as early as Nov. 13, and a debut is likely Nov. 19 or 20. Revenue for the nine months to Sept. 30 was $33.2B. The operating loss narrowed to $1.3B from $5.2B. Total commitments were $895.4B, with $69.8B due within 12 months. Nvidia, Microsoft, Google and others are buying $26B of nonvoting Class N shares.

passages.quote: Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the SEC relating to the proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock... under the symbol "ANT." The number of shares to be offered and the price range for the proposed offering have not yet been determined.
operating margins "fluctuate over time, particularly in periods when substantial incremental compute is delivered to us."
the structure "has no direct public company precedent"
Anthropic disclosed it will sell 825 million shares at "between $70 and $78 each."

caveats: Most numbers come from news coverage (CNBC, Yahoo Finance), not from the S-1 text on SEC EDGAR. Anthropic's own press release has no financials.

The commitment totals depend on how they are defined: about $417B in compute obligations (CNBC), $265.6B in noncancelable commitments, and $895.4B in total commitments (Yahoo, probably from the amended S-1). These measures are not directly comparable.
Yahoo's nine-month revenue growth figure ('$1,206%') looks like a typo and was not verified.
The price range, share count and dates come from the amended S-1 and the roadshow and may change. Final pricing and the listing date have not been announced.
The CNBC coverage I read did not describe the Long-Term Benefit Trust's role.
